widgetTool.name: show_quick_actions
widgetTool.description: Shows two to five tappable answer chips on chat: at a choice point (a disambiguation question, the verification method, the payment method, a yes or no confirmation) or as the next best actions after a major answer. Chat only; never on voice. Do not call it for the greeting itself: the opening callback adds its own page chips there. Each option is a short sentence the customer would say, because a tap sends the label back as their next message. No spoken pacing is needed. Call shape: name is always cx-show-quick-actions and all card fields go inside payload.

name.description: Always exactly cx-show-quick-actions (the card element this tool renders).

options.description: Two to five short answer labels, written the way the customer would say them.

payload.description: The card data. Put every card field inside this object.

textResponseConfig.textResponseInstruction: Write one short lead line with the exact facts the customer asked for (each amount, date or fee; when there is more than one, as short bullets that start with - and hold one fact each), then one short question. Never name or list the options in the text: the chips show them. For an identity check write only one short line such as: Quick security check. How would you like to verify? Never use an emoji for a security check, a hardship, a past due balance, a shutoff, a complaint or an error; otherwise at most one emoji at the start. This text is the whole reply, so write no other text.
